name: The Unmapping
description: A slow, politically charged flat-screen film running 187 minutes, following an elderly the Gray Zone cartographer who has spent forty years making illegal maps of GLMZ's actual infrastructure — water, power, data, bodies — as opposed to the corporate-approved city maps. Shot in real Tier 1 locations with a crew of six, the film has no dialogue for its first 45 minutes and uses found-object sound design. It has screened in seventeen underground venues and been copied thousands of times.
cultural_impact: Adopted by the Gray Zone infrastructure collectives as a training document as much as a film, and credited with inspiring three successful unauthorized water-line taps in the Tier 1 eastern district.
story_hooks: The elderly cartographer character is based on a real person, and their actual maps — rumored to be far more complete than anything shown in the film — may still exist
A corponation security contractor is quietly trying to determine how much of the film's infrastructure detail is real versus artistic license
The film's final scene depicts an entrance to an unmapped sub-basement level that several the Gray Zone residents insist they recognize
